opti-1: At dawn, every thread of a spider web holds up the others.
opti-2: In a Florida spring, a manatee drifts toward the water plants it eats.
opti-3: Sun, plants, water, fish, birds, gators. Out here, they're all tied together.
opti-4: When the rain stops, the marsh begins to dry.
opti-5: Fish crowd into the last pools, and the birds follow.
opti-6: People can cut a thread, or help tie it back.
opti-7: How are all the parts of nature, weather, plants, animals, and people, connected to each other?
33-01-welcome: Our film follows the threads that tie a marsh together. First, inspect a lumpy, furry mystery specimen.
33-01-lesson: Today you're an ecologist. Follow a river to the oysters, run the Flow Test, then trace a drought step by step.
33-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
33-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Answer with real examples, then draw your own Connection Web.
how-33-01-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the lump, then tap three things you notice.
how-33-01-compare: Put the sun under one marsh and the rain under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a marsh. Press Start the dry season. Then swap.
how-33-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing thread: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-33-01-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap something you see, then name what it connects to. Predict what happens if it changes, and see the evidence.
how-33-01-parta: For each topic, write one real-world example. Use your science words.
how-33-01-partc: Draw a Connection Web for any real ecosystem you choose. Show at least five living or nonliving things. Connect them with arrows, and write on each arrow what the connection is, like sun to sawgrass: gives light.
